facts.statement: When neurons were stimulated, the branching dendrites held vesicles still at active translation spots, while the axons sped up the movement of these vesicles.

facts.statement: A specific type of stimulation increased the share of vesicles carrying ribosomes, thereby growing the local supply of these ribosome-associated vesicles.

facts.statement: Imaging of individual mRNA molecules showed that translation sites linked to these vesicles produced about 30% more new protein signal than sites without them.

facts.statement: The results suggest these vesicles act as specialized platforms that connect neural activity signals with local protein production to control translation timing and location.
